blocks.text: Quick verdict

NodeMaven is the better choice for account-sensitive work where a flagged IP can cost you an account: its pre-screened, low-fraud-score IPs, quality guarantee and cashback are built for that, and its $2.20/GB plan rate beats IPRoyal's small-volume prices. IPRoyal is the better choice for mixed workloads that also need datacenter proxies or Web Unblocker, for single-gigabyte purchases, and for teams that want the longest documented sticky sessions. Both roll over unused residential traffic.

NodeMaven and IPRoyal are both popular with multi-account operators, anti-detect browser users and social media managers, and both keep unused traffic. NodeMaven competes on IP quality, screening every residential and mobile IP through its IP Quality Filter before assignment. IPRoyal competes on flexibility, with non-expiring residential traffic, sticky sessions up to seven days and a wider product range. This comparison helps account-focused teams decide which matters more.

blocks.text: NodeMaven in 2026: what you get

NodeMaven competes on IP quality rather than pool size. Every residential and mobile IP passes through its IP Quality Filter before it is assigned, with three strictness levels, and the company reports a 95% clean-IP rate. Proxyway's testing found the filter lowered fraud scores noticeably on sticky sessions. The pool is 30M+ residential plus 250K mobile IPs in 150+ countries, traffic rolls over, and you get up to 10% cashback on used gigabytes plus a guarantee that pays out for bad proxies.

Strengths: IP Quality Filter screens IPs before you get them; Long sticky sessions for account work; Traffic rollover and cashback; Quality guarantee that pays for bad IPs. Weak spots: Smaller pool than mass-market networks; No datacenter proxies; Pay-as-you-go rate is double the plan rate.
IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal built its reputation on flexible, non-expiring residential bandwidth and straightforward pricing. The pool is smaller than the enterprise networks at 32M+ advertised IPs, but it covers 195 countries, supports SOCKS5, and offers some of the longest sticky sessions available (up to seven days). Its headline $1.75/GB rate only applies at 10 TB; most buyers will pay between $5 and $7 per GB on small orders.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
Pricing: NodeMaven vs IPRoyal

NodeMaven charges $4.50/GB pay-as-you-go and $2.20/GB on monthly plans, with residential and mobile traffic on one balance. A $3.50 trial includes 750 MB. Unused traffic rolls over, and you earn up to 10% cashback on used traffic. ISP proxies start at $2.99 per IP with unlimited traffic.

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

For a 10 GB month, NodeMaven costs about $45 while IPRoyal costs about $52.50, so NodeMaven saves around 14%. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because IPRoyal does not publish an exact price for that volume; NodeMaven comes to about $220. Neither provider makes you use it or lose it: both NodeMaven and IPRoyal let unused traffic carry forward, so the comparison really comes down to rate and features.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

On paper the two networks are similar in size: NodeMaven advertises 30M+ residential + 250K mobile residential IPs and IPRoyal advertises 32M+. Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, NodeMaven lists 150+ countries and IPRoyal lists 195. On targeting, NodeMaven offers country, region, city and ISP, while IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, NodeMaven offers rotating or long sticky sessions (multi-day), and IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: IPRoyal wins. The deciding factor for IPRoyal: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: the quality filter matters less for high-rotation crawling.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. NodeMaven: workable, but you pay a premium for filtering you may not need. IPRoyal: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: pre-screened, low-fraud-score IPs with long sticky sessions. With IPRoyal: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. Run the same small test on both before committing.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic. How NodeMaven compares: fine for light checks.

Ad verification and geo-testing: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: good quality but a smaller pool. With IPRoyal: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Tight budgets: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires. How NodeMaven compares: mid-priced on plans, expensive on PAYG.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Verification and payment rules differ too. NodeMaven: Standard. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test NodeMaven and IPRoyal before you commit
The quickest way to choose between NodeMaven and IPRoyal is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB; IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.

3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country. 4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, NodeMaven comes out ahead in 0, IPRoyal in 3, and 3 are ties. That makes IPRoyal the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: NodeMaven is strongest for social media and multi-account management, while IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
